question: Do the full texts of PWY 2011 (KI-01/eru-0131) and PSY 2015 (KI-02/eru-0393, with KI-03/eru-0395 consulted where 2015a delegates theory to 2015b) support the agenda Rev 3 sentence 'date-stamps an explosive state in real time against derived critical values'?

PWY_2011_KI-01.criterion_a_real_time: HOLDS for the recursive ADF_r sequence: the statistic at fraction s is computed from observations 1..[ns] only, and the date-stamp is a first-crossing rule against a critical-value function fixed ex ante. Quote: 'r_e-hat = inf_{s>=r0} {s : ADF_s > cv_adf(s)}, r_f-hat = inf_{s>=r_e-hat} {s : ADF_s < cv_adf(s)}' (eq. (8), IER 52:208). FAILS for the sup statistic: 'However, sup_{r in [r0,1]} ADF_r cannot reveal the location of the exuberance' (IER 52:215) - SADF is a full-sample existence test, not a date-stamper.
PWY_2011_KI-01.criterion_b_derived_cvs: FAILS as operational source. The limit distribution of ADF_r IS derived ('Under the null we have ADF_r => [int W dW / (int W^2)^(1/2)]' , IER 52:208), but the operational date-stamping critical values are a stated convention: 'The setting employed is cv_adf_n(s) = log(log(ns))/100. For the sample sizes considered in our empirical application, this setting leads to critical values around the 4% significance level' (IER 52:208); and the test-level critical values are simulated: 'The critical values for the ADF statistic and sup_{r in [r0,1]} ADF_r are obtained by Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 replications' (Table 1 note, IER 52:214). Theory present but not the operational source -> PARTIAL by the pre-stated criterion.
PWY_2011_KI-01.statistic_attribution: Real-time property attaches to the recursive ADF_r sequence (and its rolling variant); NOT to SADF, which carries only ex-post existence evidence.

PSY_2015a_KI-02_with_KI-03.criterion_a_real_time: HOLDS for the BSADF sequence: BSADF_{r2}(r0) is computed from windows all ending at r2 (data through r2 only), and the paper states the causal split explicitly: 'Importantly, the new date-stamping strategy may be used as an ex ante real-time dating procedure, whereas the GSADF test is an ex post statistic used for analyzing a given data set for bubble behavior' (IER 56:1054). The companion (KI-03) defines both detectors on the information set I_r = {1, 2, ..., [Tr]} (IER 56:1083) and derives their real-time limit theory (Theorems 1-9). FAILS for GSADF as date-stamper: GSADF is by the authors' own statement ex post; episode dating quoted from GSADF subsamples (e.g., Table 8 subsample attributions) is full-sample.
PSY_2015a_KI-02_with_KI-03.criterion_b_derived_cvs: FAILS as operational source. Limit distributions are derived (PSY 2015a Theorem 1 eq. (5); F_{r2}(W), F_{r2}(W,r0), IER 56:1054-1055; KI-03 Theorems 1-9), but every operational quantile is simulated: 'The asymptotic critical values are obtained by numerical simulations with 2000 replications... The finite sample critical values are obtained from Monte Carlo simulation with 2000 replications' (Table 1 note, IER 56:1051); and the dating exercise: 'we compared the backward SADF statistic with the 95% SADF critical value (obtained from Monte Carlo simulations with 2,000 replications) for each observation of interest' within 'a (pseudo) real-time bubble monitoring exercise' (IER 56:1067). Theory present but not the operational source -> PARTIAL.
PSY_2015a_KI-02_with_KI-03.statistic_attribution: Real-time property attaches to BSADF_{r2}(r0) (and to the PWY ADF_{r2} special case and sequential PWY variant, per KI-03 Theorems 2-3, 8-9); NOT to GSADF, which is the ex-post summary statistic sup_{r2} BSADF_{r2}(r0).

grounds_summary: The agenda sentence quantifies over the family. Full-text reading splits it: (i) 'in real time' is SUPPORTED for the sequence statistics ADF_r (PWY) and BSADF_r2 (PSY) - each is computable at t from data through t with critical values fixed ex ante, and KI-03 proves consistency of the resulting crossing-time date estimators under cv rate conditions (cv_T -> infinity, cv_T/T^{1-alpha/2} -> 0; Theorems 2-3, 8). It is NOT supported for SADF/GSADF themselves, which both papers treat as full-sample existence tests. (ii) 'against derived critical values' is NOT supported as the operational description: in both papers the critical values actually used are Monte Carlo simulated (asymptotic-functional or finite-sample) or a stated convention (PWY log(log(ns))/100 at ~4% level); the derived limit theory delivers the distributional form and the consistency rate conditions, not the numbers. Verdict: PARTIAL per the protocol's pre-stated criterion - (a) holds for the correctly-attributed statistics, operational critical values are simulated/convention with theory present.
